verdicts.factCheck: Fetched MessageTransmitterV2.sol from circlefin/evm-cctp-contracts master. receiveMessage (lines 206-243) validates, sets usedNonces[_nonce] at line 221 and calls the recipient handler. The destination caller is enforced only when nonzero (lines 300-305). TokenMessengerV2.handleReceiveFinalizedMessage and handleReceiveUnfinalizedMessage (lines 245-283) check only that the caller is the local transmitter and that the sender is the remote token messenger, then _handleReceiveMessage (lines 405-422) mints amount minus fee to mintRecipient through BaseTokenMessenger._mintAndWithdraw (lines 330-355). hookData is never executed. v1 MessageTransmitter.sol lines 269-274 has the same zero destinationCaller rule. Circle's contract-addresses page (fetched) contains both shared v2 addresses and lists Arc, Monad, HyperEVM, X Layer, Ink, World Chain, Unichain, Polygon and Avalanche; it does not mention BNB or Robinhood. My own eth_getCode returned 2,175 bytes at both addresses on Ethereum, Base, Arc and Monad and 0 bytes on Soneium. On Arc, MessageTransmitterV2.localDomain() returns 26 and paused() returns false. balanceOf(PoolManager) on 0x3600...0000 returns 0x22fa82e0ad4 (6 decimals) and eth_getBalance of the PoolManager returns 0x1fd0149da51a004d56e6b (18 decimals), the same amount, so a native USDC mint is visible to sync and settle through the ERC-20 face.
verdicts.codeCheck: sync needs no unlock and stores currency and balanceOf(PoolManager) in transient slots (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). _settle reads the synced currency, rejects msg.value for an ERC-20, and credits balanceOf minus the synced reserves to the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). take debits the delta and transfers (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), and unlock requires a zero delta count at the end (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), which is met after take. No guard ties the balance increase to the settler. Any mint to the PoolManager that happens between the caller's sync and settle is credited to that caller.
verdicts.corrections: The handler reached on v2 is handleReceiveFinalizedMessage or handleReceiveUnfinalizedMessage depending on finalityThresholdExecuted (MessageTransmitterV2.sol lines 223-241), which both call _handleReceiveMessage. The victim is a bridger who chose the PoolManager as mintRecipient, which is an unusual act; no LP or ERC-6909 holder funds are exposed, so low is right. BNB Smart Chain and Robinhood Chain carry the code but are not listed as Circle domains; that agrees with the finding.

verdicts.factCheck: Fetched the cited sources. OP CrossDomainMessenger.relayMessage (develop) lets a caller other than the remote messenger relay a message only when failedMessages[versionedHash] is set (lines 239-248) and with msg.value zero; StandardBridge.finalizeBridgeERC20 (lines 272-299) mints or safeTransfers to _to and its onlyOtherBridge check (lines 111-117) is satisfied because relayMessage sets xDomainMsgSender to _sender before the call (line 284). OptimismPortal2.finalizeWithdrawalTransactionExternalProof (lines 701-730) is public and takes the proof submitter as an argument. AbsOutbox.executeTransaction (lines 158-174) has no caller restriction. PolygonZkEVMBridgeV2.claimAsset at v9.0.0 (line 453 onward) carries only ifNotEmergencyState. StateReceiver.replayFailedStateSync and replayFailedStateSyncWithData (lines 85-103) have no caller restriction. TeleporterMessenger._checkIsAllowedRelayer (lines 596-613) admits any relayer for an empty list. eth_getCode at 0x...1001 on Polygon and at 0x4200...0007 on OP Mainnet returned contract code.
verdicts.codeCheck: Same accounting path as finding 0: sync without unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), balance difference credited to the settler (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364), take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), delta count check at the end of unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Native value paths are not affected because native is credited only as msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354) and src/ has no receive or fallback outside src/test.
verdicts.corrections: OptimismPortal2 on develop now also has a bridge hook that can hold a withdrawal (doc comment above line 701); the deployed mainnet portal version was not checked, but finalizeWithdrawalTransactionExternalProof has been public with an arbitrary proof submitter since it was introduced. No pending item paying a PoolManager was found by the author or by me, so the hazard is an integration hazard only; low is right.

clearedSpotChecks.check: ERC-4337 handleOps as a carrier that runs several accounts' code in one transaction: can an ordinary account place operations before and after another user's payment to the PoolManager and book it.
clearedSpotChecks.note: EntryPoint v0.7 handleOps (lines 174-200) is public with nonReentrant and runs each op as a separate call. An attacker op can call sync outside an unlock, but a victim who pays inside its own unlock calls sync itself, which overwrites the slots (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), and settles before its call returns. Only a victim who sends tokens to the PoolManager before or outside its own sync is exposed, and that is already lost surplus.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2: balance changes without a transfer call between two frames of one transaction that an ordinary account could book with sync and settle.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Native is credited only as msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354) and grep of src/ finds receive and fallback only in src/test. ERC-20 face inflows inside an attacker transaction come from the attacker's own funds or from third-party relays, which findings 0 and 1 cover.
